info.name: SRMS — Smart Restaurant Management System (Assignment 2)
info.description:
REST API for the Smart Restaurant Management System.

Run the server first: `cd server && npm run db:reset && npm run dev` (MySQL must be running).

Run **00 Setup → Log in (customer)** and **Log in (admin)** once: they store `customerToken` and `adminToken` as collection variables, and every guarded request uses them.

The collection is ordered top to bottom: health, auth, menu, users, orders, reservations, events, admin reporting, AI, then the error cases. Running the whole collection exercises every endpoint and leaves the demo database in a sensible state.

item.name: 00 Health & discovery
item.description: Nothing to authenticate: these confirm the server, the database connection and the API index are up.

request.description: Reports `connected`, `not connected` or the MySQL error code. Use this to prove the database layer is wired up.

item.name: 01 Auth
item.description: Registering an account and getting the session tokens the rest of the collection uses. Demo logins are seeded: admin@srms.dev and demo@srms.dev, password demo1234.

request.description: Duplicate e-mail addresses come back as 409, and a short password as 422 — see the Errors folder.

item.name: Register with a password that is too short
Log in with the wrong password

exec: pm.test('the message does not say which half was wrong', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.code).to.eql('UNAUTHORIZED'); pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.message).to.eql('Email or password is incorrect'));

item.name: 02 Menu (public browse, admin edit)
item.description: Browsing and filtering happens in SQL, so the filters scale with the table. Only an administrator may change the menu.

exec: pm.test('everything matches the filters', () => pm.response.json().items.forEach((item) => { pm.expect(item.category).to.eql('main'); pm.expect(item.dietaryTags).to.include('vegetarian'); }));
pm.test('facet lists are built from the data', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().dietaryTags).to.include('gluten-free'));

body.raw:
{
  "name": "Postman Special Pizza",
  "category": "main",
  "price": 15.5,
  "description": "Created by the Postman collection so it can be updated and deleted again.",
  "ingredients": [
    "flour",
    "tomato",
    "mozzarella"
  ],
  "allergens": [
    "gluten",
    "dairy"
  ],
  "dietaryTags": [
    "vegetarian"
  ],
  "available": true,
  "todaySpecial": false,
  "emoji": "🍕"
}

item.name: A customer may not add a dish
03 Users & favourites
item.description: Customers manage their own profile and favourites; an administrator can list and moderate every account.

exec: pm.test('no password hash in the response', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.not.have.property('password_hash'));
pm.test('the saved dishes come back in order', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().favourites.map((d) => d.id)).to.eql([1, 2, 3]));

item.name: Read my own profile by id
An administrator cannot change their own role

exec: pm.test('the guard is explained', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.message).to.match(/cannot change your own role/i));

item.name: A customer cannot change a role
You cannot delete your own account

exec: pm.test('the refusal is explained', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.message).to.match(/signed in with/i));

item.name: 04 Orders
item.description: Prices are never taken from the client: send dish ids and quantities, the server looks up the price and works out the subtotal, delivery fee and tax.

exec: pm.test('the totals are calculated by the server', () => { const order = pm.response.json().order; pm.expect(order.subtotal).to.be.above(0); pm.expect(Number((order.subtotal + order.deliveryFee + order.tax).toFixed(2))).to.eql(order.total); });

request.description: No token: the order is scoped to the guest contact details and can be looked up by reference.

item.name: Look up an order by reference

request.description: The reference is what the customer gets by email. A guest reads a guest order with the reference plus the email it was placed with.

exec: pm.test('the line items come back with the snapshot prices', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().order.items).to.be.an('array').that.isNotEmpty());
pm.test('the workflow is enforced', () => { pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.code).to.eql('INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION'); pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.message).to.match(/cannot go from/); });
pm.test('sentiment is left for the analysis step', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().feedback.sentiment).to.be.null);

item.name: 05 Reservations
item.description: Availability is worked out against the table sizes, the opening hours and the existing bookings. Double booking is prevented inside a database transaction.

exec: pm.test('the tables fit the party', () => pm.response.json().tables.forEach((t) => pm.expect(t.seats).to.be.at.least(4)));

item.name: Book the same table in the same slot

exec: pm.test('the clash is reported, not silently accepted', () => { pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.code).to.eql('TABLE_ALREADY_BOOKED'); pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.message).to.match(/already booked/); });

request.description: The table assigned to the booking above is asked for again in the same slot — this is the double-booking guard.

exec: pm.test('the party size changed and the table was re-checked', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().reservation.partySize).to.eql(2));

item.name: 06 Special events
item.description:
Birthday, corporate and group bookings share the reservation model, with the occasion, requirements and a pre-selected menu.

Events are returned under the same `reservation` key as ordinary bookings, and the response key is the same `/api/reservations` shape.

Folders 05 and 06 use fixed dates in 2030, so run `npm run db:reset` in the server before a full collection run, otherwise the bookings from the previous run are still in the way.

body.raw:
{
  "date": "2030-04-02",
  "startTime": "18:00",

item.name: Add the catering notes while it is still pending

exec: pm.test('the notes were saved', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().reservation.requirements).to.eql('Two vegetarian plates'));

item.name: A customer cannot change an approved booking

exec: pm.test('the rule is explained', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.message).to.match(/can only be changed by the restaurant/i));

item.name: 07 Admin reporting
item.description: Everything is produced by SQL aggregates, and cancelled orders are excluded from revenue and popularity.

exec: pm.test('the numbers add up', () => { const body = pm.response.json(); const sum = body.statusBreakdown.filter((r) => r.status !== 'cancelled').reduce((a, r) => a + r.revenue, 0); pm.expect(Number(sum.toFixed(2))).to.eql(body.orders.revenue); });
pm.test('one point per day, gaps filled in', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().series).to.have.lengthOf(14));
pm.test('sorted by quantity', () => { const q = pm.response.json().items.map((i) => i.quantity); pm.expect(q).to.eql([...q].sort((a, b) => b - a)); });
pm.test('each row names the order and the customer', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().feedback[0]).to.have.property('orderReference'));

item.name: A customer may not read the figures
08 AI assistant & feedback analysis
item.description: The assistant answers from live database rows. Sign in first, and the personal questions work too.

item.name: Ask: what did I order last time?

exec: pm.test('the answer comes from the orders table', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().sources).to.include('orders'));
pm.test('a real free slot is offered', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().text).to.match(/free on/));
pm.test('the fallback offers the suggested questions', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().suggestedQuestions).to.not.be.empty);

item.name: Ask an external model for the brief

exec: pm.test('falls back to the local brief when no key is set', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().generatedBy).to.be.a('string'));

item.name: 09 Errors & rules
item.description: The shape of the answers when something goes wrong — the same envelope for every failure.

item.name: A token that has been edited
Unknown dish id in an order

exec: pm.test('the message names the problem', () => { pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.code).to.eql('CART_NOT_ORDERABLE'); pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.message).to.match(/cannot be ordered/i); });
